channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Joshua Palmer (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
item.description: Palmer practiced in a red non-contact jersey on Thursday. Even if he plays this week, he is likely only relevant in single-game DFS tournaments. He mostly provides Josh Allen with another viable target on a couple of plays.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
item.description: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia notes that Moore resumed practicing today after sitting out on Wednesday and Thursday. He did the same thing last week before being labeled questionable and ultimately ruled out on game day. It looks like he’s a game-time decision again this week. If active, he can be started as a WR2, but re-injury remains a risk.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Free agent Terrell Jennings worked out for the Patriots on Friday.
item.description: Free agent running backs Ulysses Bentley and Josh Pitsenberger also worked out for the Patriots. TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Jets. Perhaps the Patriots are making backup plans.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Elijah Arroyo (shoulder) underwent further testing on Friday.
item.description: No update yet on what was learned, and we may have to wait until next week’s first injury report to learn more. The Seahawks’ young tight end has faced multiple injuries in his short career. Hopefully, this one is not serious.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold’s starting quarterback job is not in jeopardy.
item.description: The Seahawks’ head coach stood by his quarterback today, saying Darnold is “definitely part of the solution” to the offense’s recent struggles. Darnold returned somewhat quickly from a glute tendon strain a couple of weeks ago. One wonders if he is still rounding back into form following the early-season ailment. Backup Drew Lock played well in his stead, but the Seahawks believe their Super Bowl-winning quarterback should keep his job. That makes sense to us. He’s a QB2 next week against the Chiefs.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Davis Allen (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
item.description: He got in a limited session and the Rams apparently trust him to play despite a pair of missed practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Colby Parkinson (shoulder) also avoided the final report. Tyler Higbee is the Rams tight end you should be using at this point.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Lions placed Ben Bartch on injured reserve with a foot injury.
item.description: The Lions lose one of their top backup offensive lineman and LB Devin White (forearm) to injured reserve. Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters post-game last week that White would likely require surgery.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Budda Baker (groin) is questionable for Arizona’s Week 6 game against the Rams.
item.description: It was a pop-up DNP for Baker on Friday after he had initially been listed as NIR-Rest on Wednesday. Ominous. Baker stands a real chance at missing Sunday’s game and throwing the Cardinals defense into (checking notes)furtherchaos against the Rams.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Josh Downs (hamstring/rest) is not on Indianapolis’ final Week 6 injury report.
item.description: Given how Downs’ season is going, it’s hard to believe he’s going to do much with the extra runway, but Tyler Warren (groin) popping up on the report could shift more targets to Downs and Keenan Allen on Sunday against the Titans.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Tyler Warren (groin) is questionable for Indianapolis’ Week 6 game against the Titans.
item.description: Warren popped up on the injury report on Friday after suffering the injury in practice. Fantasy managers who were relying on Warren likely won’t find a good enough option to replace him with proactively on waivers at this point, so it makes some sense to sit and wait for more reporting to come out or for him to be ruled out. This was, frankly, the last thing the Colts needed given how banged up their receiving corps has been.-Rivers McCown
